name: Finolex Cables Ltd
tagline: Debt-free, cash-rich electrical-cables brand (~Rs 19,400 Cr) with a genuine high-operating-leverage inflection in its small optical-fibre-cable segment (data-centre/5G demand), but the OFC business is only ~8% of revenue and a long-running promoter family feud is the reason it trades at a discount to peers
business_overview: Finolex Cables makes electrical wires & cables (the bulk of revenue - housing wire, power cables) and communication cables (optical fibre cable / OFC, historically a primary supplier to Jio and Airtel). It is backward-integrating into OFC preforms and expanding fibre-draw capacity. Near debt-free with ~Rs 2,500 Cr of liquid investments. Associate stake in Finolex Industries (PVC pipes) - the two companies are linked to the disputing Chhabria cousins.
fundamentals_table: ROCE ~21% / 3-yr ROE ~13% (large idle-cash pile drags ROE)
Revenue CAGR ~13%; TTM revenue ~Rs 6,300 Cr; Q3 FY26 revenue +35% YoY; electrical-wire volumes +~28% in that quarter, OFC volumes +~34%
Electrical margin +~230 bps in Q1 FY27 (7% volume growth); communication segment profit jumped from ~Rs 1.3 Cr to ~Rs 52.5 Cr on Rs 176 Cr revenue
Debt-free; ~Rs 2,500 Cr liquid investments; life-high capex ~Rs 500 Cr on preform/fibre
Trades at a persistent discount to Polycab and other peers; 52-week range Rs 701 - 1,204
fundamentals_narrative: The core electrical business is a solid ~13% grower with a strong brand, debt-free balance sheet and a large cash pile (which depresses ROE to ~13% despite ~21% ROCE). The interesting development is the communication (OFC) segment: Q1 FY27 revenue +62% to ~Rs 176 Cr with segment profit rising from ~Rs 1.3 Cr to ~Rs 52.5 Cr - textbook operating leverage - on data-centre / AI / 5G / broadband demand that members say the market has been ignoring in favour of HFCL and Sterlite. Capacity is doubling (OFC 4 to 8 mkm; preform for ~4 mkm in-house, rest sourced), with a value-add push toward higher-fibre-count cables for DC/AI. But OFC is still only ~8% of the business, helium/germanium input sourcing is a risk (West Asia war, China curbs), and the unresolved promoter feud / lack of clear owner leadership is a structural reason the stock is cheap versus peers.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Wide 52-week range (Rs 701-1,204); a margin bounce-back on the Q1 FY27 print, but the stock has structurally lagged Polycab for years.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent ~14 of 68 posts (Nov 2022 to Aug 2026). Amit_Agarwal1 (non-trusted, invested, long-time tracker) is the main voice - documented the promoter feud escalating into 'an all-out war between the cousins', Deepak Chhabria's removal as Executive Chairman, and the lack of succession planning as the reason the market values it at <15x despite the brand; but also flags the Q1 FY27 communication-segment 'real kicker' the market is ignoring. karanshah137 (elevated) posted (Mar 2026) that management sees robust OFC demand for data centres and can gain share from Sterlite Tech and HFCL - constructive, not a hard buy call. Niraj_Punjkaran (elevated) posted detailed Q1 FY27 concall notes: 'subdued bullishness' on the fibre opportunity (currently ~8%), 100 MT preform from Q3, OFC capacity 4 to 8 mkm by Aug 31, an alluded ~Rs 300 Cr MRR from fibre, and an export-business-development push (Rs 30-40 Cr OFC sales to US/EU clients in Q1). Aman_Jain3 detailed the raw-material (helium/germanium) sourcing risk.
community_signal: Two elevated members (karanshah137, Niraj_Punjkaran) are constructive specifically on the OFC / data-centre optionality, but both frame it as an emerging opportunity to watch (~8% of the business), not a high-conviction buy. The dominant thread narrative remains the promoter feud discount.
bse_notes: Long-running Chhabria family dispute (Supreme Court / NCLT); founder's gift-deed of controlling stake contested; Deepak Chhabria removed as Executive Chairman (2023) - no clear line of succession, cited repeatedly as the valuation discount driver. Debt-free with ~Rs 2,500 Cr investments; ~Rs 500 Cr preform/fibre capex. Helium and germanium input-sourcing risk. No SEBI action; no red-flag tier.
bull_case: Genuine high-operating-leverage inflection in OFC - Q1 FY27 segment profit ~Rs 1.3 Cr to ~Rs 52.5 Cr - on DC/AI/5G/broadband demand the market has under-appreciated vs HFCL/Sterlite
Debt-free, cash-rich (~Rs 2,500 Cr), strong consumer-electrical brand, ~21% ROCE
OFC capacity doubling with backward integration into preform and a value-add / export push
Trades at a persistent discount to peers - a feud resolution would be a re-rating catalyst
bear_case: Large-cap (~Rs 19,400 Cr) growing ~13% overall - a 10x needs a ~Rs 1.94 lakh Cr valuation, not credible
The OFC inflection, while real, is only ~8% of revenue - too small relative to the base to move the whole company multiple-fold
Unresolved promoter feud and no succession plan - the structural reason for the discount, no timeline for resolution
Idle cash drags ROE to ~13%; helium/germanium sourcing risk for the preform ramp
verdict_headline: 'Neither' - a debt-free quality franchise with a real but too-small OFC inflection, capped by a large base and an unresolved promoter feud; worth watching for the fibre ramp, not a 10x candidate
verdict_reasoning: At ~Rs 19,400 Cr and ~13% overall growth, neither a 10x-in-2-3-years nor 100x-in-10 outcome is credible - the OFC operating-leverage story is genuine but ~8% of revenue, not enough to re-rate the whole company multiple-fold
The promoter family feud and absent succession plan are a standing discount with no resolution timeline
Elevated members are constructive on the OFC optionality but explicitly frame it as an emerging watch-item, not a conviction buy
No red-flag tier; no 30-day revisit. Re-check if the OFC segment scales toward a double-digit share of revenue/profit or the family dispute resolves

trusted_signals.note: Detailed Q1 FY27 concall notes - 'subdued bullishness' on the optical-fibre opportunity (currently ~8% of business), 100 MT preform from Q3, OFC capacity 4 to 8 mkm by end-Aug, ~Rs 300 Cr MRR alluded to from fibre, export-BD push (Rs 30-40 Cr OFC to US/EU in Q1). Constructive tracking, not a buy call.

Management sees fairly robust demand for optical-fibre cables in data centres; company can gain market share from Sterlite Tech and HFCL. Constructive on the OFC optionality; not a hard conviction call.

four_box.note: Verdict explicit: 'OFC operating-leverage story is genuine' (tailwind=yes) but ~8% of revenue, 'not enough to re-rate the whole company multiple-fold' (tam=no); promoter family feud is a standing, unresolved discount.
